Notes: Mayor Mncedisi Maphisa was suspended in February 2023, and was recalled by the IFP the following month.
The ABC withdrew from this government in April 2023 on a directive from its president, Philani Mavundla. The government continued without it.

Castro De Bruin was elected mayor seven votes to five, one councillor excused. Two votes came from DA councillors, and we could not establish which two of the PA, GOOD and KDF joined the ANC, so all three are coded Unknown.

Mayor Gideon Pietersen was replaced by Thershia Prince of the PA, who resigned on 31 January 2023. Ashley Sauls of the PA was elected mayor in February 2023. By-elections in June 2024 took the DA from four seats to seven of thirteen, an outright majority, which it then used the following month to vote this coalition out.
Speaker N. P. Yantolo-Nkonyeni was replaced by E. A. Miggels of the EFF, the party's only councillor. We could not establish the date on which this occurred.
Mayor Paul Swart was removed by a council vote in May 2024. Deputy Mayor Raymond Ross then acted in the office, and was elected mayor in June 2024.
Mayor Ruben Richards resigned in June 2025 and Azrial Scheepers of the ANC was elected. Scheepers had already replaced Andre Mouton as deputy mayor earlier that year.

By-elections in April and August 2024 moved two ANC seats, one to the CFRA and one to the DA, taking this government from the six it needed for a majority to eight. The seat cells record the council as it formed.

Mayor Sivuyile Ngodwana was removed by a council vote in March 2024, the coalition's smaller partners voting with an opposition motion. Two sittings then failed to elect a successor, and the province warned it would consider intervening. N. Xhakaza of the ANC was elected in April.

Murunwa Makwarela left the speakership to take the mayoralty, so the speakership is recorded as Vacant. This government lasted ten days, too short to observe the PA, AIC and RCoT, which are coded Unknown.
The ABC, the CFP and the DA are coded Unknown. The motion that formed this government needed at least four votes beyond the IFP's nine, and we found no source recording how any party voted.

Speaker Sbusiso Myaka was removed by a council vote in December 2024 and S. Ndlela of the IFP, an opposition party, was elected in his place. No new government followed, and an office won against one does not make its holder a partner.
During this period, a by-election in March 2023 replaced an independent councillor with one from the IFP, taking the IFP from eight seats to nine.

This government ended in September 2025 when the council elected a new mayor and speaker under a national intervention. The termination value names dissolution, but the council was not dissolved and stayed in place.

The motion that formed this government carried without objection and the mayor was elected unopposed, so no vote was recorded by party. The ANC is coded Unknown. Speaker R. Matlholoa held the office in an acting capacity. J. Modisakeng was in the chair by January 2025, and we could not establish the date of the change or his party.
The FF Plus joined the mayoral committee in about July 2023, after this government formed. The role cells record the relationships at formation.
Mayor Siyabonga Ndlovu resigned in November 2024 after the DA filed a no-confidence motion, and M. Mkhize, also of the IFP, was elected later that month.
The MSA voted with the government at the one confidence division held in this period and is recorded at no other. It is coded Unknown.
Al Jama-ah, the DLC and the MSA each voted with the government once and were absent when it was next tested; KZNI voted with it once and against it once. All four are coded Unknown.
The mayor and deputy mayor were elected by secret ballot, so the vote carries no party attribution. Seventeen smaller parties are coded Unknown on that account.
The mayor recorded here was elected in October 2023, when the sittings that installed this government were repeated. We could not find the name of the councillor installed in August.
Three of the fifty-five seats were vacant when this government formed. All three were filled by by-elections in January and February 2026, and the Patriotic Alliance won all three.
By-elections in July 2023 took the DA to twenty-eight of fifty-five seats, an outright majority, and it governed alone from then. The seat cells record the council as it formed.
The EFF opposed this government when it formed, but switched over to supporting it during the term. The role cells record the relationships at formation.
A by-election in June 2023 moved a seat from the IFP to the ANC during this government, taking the IFP and DA together below the votes needed to carry a motion.

Speaker Nobuhle Mthembu was removed by a council vote in June 2025 and Margaret Arnolds of the AIC was elected in her place the following month. The council created the city's first deputy mayor post in January 2026. Masuku was elected to it on 26 February 2026.
Mayor Thapelo Amad resigned in April 2023 and Kabelo Gwamanda of Al Jama-ah was elected eleven days later. A June 2023 by-election moved a seat from the ANC to the PA.
This government lasted under a month, too short for several parties to be observed in a role. The AIC, ATM, PAC and UDM are all coded as Unknown.
Deputy Mayor Werner Meshoa was replaced by Ruiters, also of ICOSA. We could not establish the date on which this occurred.
The ANC withdrew from the coalition in December 2021 and directed its councillors to the opposition benches, keeping the speakership. It is coded Opposition.
A by-election in June 2022 took a seat from the ANC to the DA, lifting this government one seat above a majority. The seat cells record the council as it formed.
We could not find a minute or report of the installation vote, but the DA's two seats could not have carried it alone. The ANC, PA and FF Plus are all coded Unknown.
The FF Plus was given the speakership when this government formed, which rules out opposition but does not show whether it governed as a partner or supported from outside. It is coded Unknown.
This government lasted sixteen days and no council sitting fell inside it, so the DA, PA and FF Plus are all coded Unknown.
A by-election in December 2024 caused a seat to shift from the DA to the ANC during this government, giving the ANC six of eleven seats and a majority on its own.
A by-election in October 2024 moved a seat from the DA to the ANC during this government, giving the ANC six of eleven seats. The DA and COPE continued to govern for another 47 days.

Deputy Mayor Alberto Marbi of the PBI resigned in March 2025. Speaker Mncedisi Skosana was removed as a councillor in May 2025 and the speakership fell with his seat; Mark Willemse of the Knysna Independent Movement replaced him.

Mayor Fuzile Jan Yake's surname is spelled Yakhe in the ANC's own announcement of his candidacy. By-elections in September and November 2025 moved two ANC seats to the PA. This took this coalition from the seven seats recorded here to five out of twelve, below a majority. Speaker Dadley Maasdorp was removed by a council vote in December 2025, and Sharon Ferguson of the FF Plus became acting speaker.
Mayor Lindi Nhaca was removed by a council vote in October 2024. Muzi Ali Ngidi of the ANC was elected mayor days later, with Njabulo Cele as deputy mayor.
Evidence of the ANC's relationship to this government points different ways, and we could not definitively establish whether it is government or opposition. The ANC is therefore coded Unknown.
The mayoralty changed twice inside this government. Mitchell John Smith gave way to Johanna Botha of the ANC in 2022, and Botha to Amanda Kleinbooi of the PA in 2023.
Speaker Dumisani Msibi resigned in June 2025 and Phindile Mahlaba was elected in his place. We could not establish Mahlaba's party.
Mayor Masechaba Mosia-Lakaje was recalled by the ANC and resigned in June 2024. Malekula Melato of the ANC was elected mayor in her place.
The PA's ward councillor left for the DA in May 2022, leaving the DA and FF Plus one short of a majority on the seven seats recorded here. A July by-election gave the DA the seat and the majority.

Mayor Danny Thupane resigned in October 2024 and L. G. Sele of the ANC, the sitting speaker, was elected mayor. D. David of the ANC became speaker. An IFP councillor took the new post of deputy executive mayor in November 2024.

The Coalitions Barometer 2021-2023 describes an ANC support bloc without naming its members, so the ABC, ACDP, AIC, JEP, PA and the independent councillor are coded Unknown. Ward 2 moved to the IFP in March 2023 and back to the ANC in December 2024.

A by-election in February 2023 moved a second seat from the ANC to the IFP during this government, taking the IFP from twenty seats to twenty-one. The seat cells record the council as it formed. Nothile Mthethwa (EFF) was deputy mayor in February 2023, after the EFF instructed its deputy mayors to resign. M. Z. Shobede was deputy mayor at 30 June 2024.
A by-election in January 2023 caused a seat to switch from the ANC to the IFP during this government, taking the IFP from nineteen seats to twenty.
Mayor Nozililo Ntema was removed from office by a council vote in April 2025 and an acting mayor was elected at the same sitting. We could not find any authoritative source naming that person.

A by-election in May 2025 moved a seat from the NCM to the ANC during this government, leaving the DA and NCM together one short of a majority. Mayor Gustav Bock and Speaker Rodney Kritzinger exchanged offices in June 2024 under a rotation agreed between the NCM and the DA in 2021.
In October 2024 Mayor Gary van Niekerk and Deputy Mayor Babalwa Lobishe resigned and were each elected to the other's office.
The EFF withdrew its support at the end of January 2023 after an announcement by Julius Malema, and this government continued without it. By-elections during 2024 moved seats from the ANC to the IFP.
A by-election in February 2026 took a seat from the NFP to the IFP. The seat cells record the council as it formed.
By-elections in February 2022 moved a seat from the IFP to the NFP during this government, taking the IFP to twenty seats and the NFP to fourteen.
Deputy Mayor Mlandeli Nyuka resigned in November 2022 and Vlancio Donson of ICOSA was elected in his place. Both parties remained in the coalition.
ICOSA left this government in April 2022 when a council vote removed its deputy mayor, and Leon Campher of AK was elected in his place.
Mayor T. B. Afrika was replaced by W. Harmse, also of the ANC. We could not establish the exact date on which this occurred or the reason why it happened.

Mayor Gladys Khoza resigned in October 2023 and W. M. Matsheke, also of the ANC, was elected in her place. Nontombi Molatlhegi was elected to the new post of deputy executive mayor on 1 December 2023.
The deputy mayoralty was vacant at formation, and Charmaine Laubscher of the DA filled it five weeks later. Mayor Andre Truter stepped down at the end of January 2026.
Mayor K. D. Sonyoni and Speaker N. N. Maputle were both recalled in December 2024. M. Bartlett and D. Peters, both of the ANC, were elected in their places.
Speaker Thomas Mpye resigned the chair in August 2023 while remaining a councillor. He co-sponsored a motion against Mayor Petros Masilela.
One of the eleven seats was vacant when this government formed. Speaker J. van Schalkwyk resigned his seat in February 2025 and J. du T. Loubser, also of the FF Plus, was elected in his place.

GOOD expelled its three councillors nine days after this government formed, leaving the speakership vacant until November 2024. Mayor Theunis Zimmermann's surname is spelled Zimmerman in court judgments.
S. Shuma was deputy executive mayor from August 2024, after the administration took office.

Contemporaneous reporting places the EFF in conflict with this government at its first sitting, and a later retrospective places it inside the founding coalition. Both Coalitions Barometer volumes leave it open, so the EFF is coded Unknown. Mayor Karel Papier died in office in August 2023 and Mary Liebenberg, also of the PA, was elected in his place in September.

Mayor Leonard Makenna and Speaker Danny Jonas were removed by a council vote in December 2021, and a court set that vote aside and returned both in January 2022. The Coalitions Barometer 2021-2023 prints his given name Leornard.
Mayor Sibongile Khathi resigned to take a provincial post and Deputy Mayor Mthandeni Mbutho acted from September 2023. A July 2022 by-election moved a seat from the DA to the ANC.
By-elections in April 2023 and February 2025 each moved a seat from the ANC to the IFP during this government, taking the IFP to seventeen seats and the ANC to sixteen.
The Coalitions Barometer 2023-2025 is silent on the NFP's role while other sources list it as a member, so the NFP is coded Unknown. A September 2023 by-election moved a seat from the ANC to the IFP.
The Coalitions Barometer 2021-2023 names the blocs on either side of this council, but does not place the NFP in either of them. It is therefore coded as Unknown.

A by-election in September 2022 moved a seat from the ANC to the IFP during this government, taking the IFP from twenty-three seats to twenty-four. Mayor Nkonzoyakhe Dando resigned two weeks after taking office and Xolani Ngwezi, also of the IFP, was elected in December 2021.
A by-election in October 2022 moved a seat from Al Jama-ah to the IFP during this government, taking the IFP from five seats to six.

A by-election in June 2024 moved a seat from the ABC to the IFP during this government, taking the IFP to eleven seats and the ABC to six. The ANC's provincial leadership directed its councillors to break with the IFP in October 2025. No withdrawal was completed and the ANC speaker continued to convene the council.
A by-election in June 2023 moved a seat from the ANC to the IFP during this government, taking the IFP to ten seats and the ANC to nine.
Mayor Katriena Robyn's given name is spelled Katrina in the Coalitions Barometer 2023-2025. Her party's spelling is used here.
Speaker Johnnerey Mouton was removed by a council vote in May 2022, and Elizabeth Sidego of the DA replaced him. Deputy Mayor Katriena Robyn gave way to Felicity Klazen of GOOD.
